title: Jonathan Gruber — MIT 14.01 Lecture 9 handout: market equilibrium and consumer/producer surplus, Fall 2023
use: Primary graphical teaching reference for clearing, shifts and consumer/producer-surplus areas; original algebra and existence conditions are supplied in the chapter.
verification: Retrieved the official 13-page handout and inspected extracted labels for Figures 9-1 through 9-12, including clearing, shifts, consumer and producer surplus, and output restriction. This is a graphical method route, not a proof source for every regularity condition. Original numbers, examples and exercise solutions are independently derived.

title: MIT 14.581 International Economics I — Lecture 24: Trade Policy Theory (II), Spring 2013, slides 10–12
use: Scoped primary reference for quasilinear preferences, numeraire normalization, income/transfer plus surplus decomposition, and a partial-equilibrium interpretation.
verification: Read the preference/numeraire and indirect-utility setup on PDF pages 10–12 (slides 10–12), including the consumer surplus term and government transfer. The chapter adds explicit nonbinding numeraire conditions and original one-market derivations. No claim is made to teach or verify the subsequent political-economy equilibrium.

title: Frank Levy — A Note on the Tax Incidence Problem, MIT 11.203, 19 September 2010
use: Primary route for the buyer/seller price wedge and matched quantity changes underlying tax incidence.
verification: Read all three substantive pages of the four-page official note. The chapter derives its own differential formula and labels point-elasticity shares as local at an initially untaxed equilibrium; it does not treat constant initial elasticities as an exact arbitrary nonlinear finite-tax rule. No source numerical example is reproduced.

title: OpenStax Principles of Microeconomics 3e — 8.3 Entry and Exit Decisions in the Long Run
use: Primary open-textbook method route for competitive entry/exit and constant-, increasing- and decreasing-cost industries.
verification: Read the entry/exit and industry-type sections. The chapter supplies original global-average-cost derivations and integer-firm counterexample, states identical-technology/constant-input-price assumptions, and distinguishes constant industry input prices from constant returns at every firm output. No historical business-count or empirical industry claim is imported.
